messages.author: 67ad43f188b9c5e7
messages.subject: DIF; significance level?
parts:
Hi Phil,

Thank-you so much for developing the mirt package! 

I was replicating the R example codes in mirt package to conduct DIF analyses. 

#DIF test for each item (using all other items as anchors)
itemnames <- colnames(data)
refmodel <- multipleGroup(data, models, group = group1, SE=TRUE,
                          invariance=c('free_means', 'free_var', itemnames))
#loop over items (in practice, run in parallel to increase speed). May be better to use ?DIF
estmodels <- vector('list', ncol(CONTROL_dem_ethnic))
for(i in 1:ncol(data))
  estmodels[[i]] <- multipleGroup(data, models, group = group1, verbose = FALSE, calcNull=FALSE,
                                  invariance=c('free_means', 'free_var', itemnames[-i]))
(anovas <- lapply(estmodels, anova, object2=refmodel, verbose=FALSE))
#family-wise error control
p <- do.call(rbind, lapply(anovas, function(x) x[2, 'p']))
p.adjust(p, method = 'BH') ### NO DIF items


I wonder, after obtaining the p-values for the last step (i.e. the adjusted p-values), what level of significance (p=0.05, p=0.01, etc.) should I use to decide a DIF item, thus to proceed DRF() analyses? Do you have any suggested reference for that? 

Many thanks!
Yingyi

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: DIF; significance level?
parts:
The last line is controlling for family-wise error, so you can still be generally exploratory and use something like p < .05. I'm a little more on the conservative side though and would probably go lower, like .01, but there really is no hard limits here. That's partially why information criteria are useful too (which really can be interpreted as different transformations of the p-value in the direction of preferring lower p-values instead of higher ones).

Phil
